path_class_justification.correction_note: An earlier draft of this matrix said the protected route returns 401 for the missing authorization; the code maps localbAuthorizationUnavailable to 503. 401 is only reached after authorization is configured and the client proof headers are missing/ill-formed. Corrected 2026-10-23.
path_class_justification.evidence: SimiGo/Protocol/HTTPServer.swift: localbRoutePolicy(forMethod:routePath:) maps POST /v1/chat/completions to .protected(permission: .inference) (line 1186-1191). verifyLOCALBProtectedRequest (line 1320-1334) then fails closed in order: (a) guard context.transportSecurity.eligibleForLOCALBPairingBinding (== isTLS, line 213) else localbTransportNotTrusted -> HTTP 403 'Protected requests require a LOCALB TLS connection'; (b) guard let authorization = localbRequestAuthorization else localbAuthorizationUnavailable -> HTTP 503 'LOCALB request authorization is not configured'; (c) x-simigo-localb-client-key-id + 32-byte x-simigo-localb-challenge + 64-byte x-simigo-localb-proof-v2 required else localbRequestRejected(401) LOCALB_CLIENT_PROOF_MISSING; (d) authorization.coordinator.authorizeProtectedRequest(..., checkpoint:) must accept the proof against a paired client key and trusted checkpoint. NativeMLX.startWithLOCALB with localbRequestAuthorization=nil only calls server.configureLOCALBTransport(identity:) (NativeMLX.swift:487-502) and never configureLOCALBRequestAuthorization, so the generateHandler wired at NativeMLX.swift:422-480 is unreachable over the wire from a standalone headless process: it would need a LOCALB TLS-paired client key plus a per-request signature, i.e. a second product surface outside the process under test.
path_class_justification.priority: §2 requires preferring Service/HTTPServer dispatch; verified before accepting the fallback.

timestamp_precision_regression_fixed_202.fix: Lossless timestamp codec in SimiGoESISDatabase: persist `timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate` (the exact value `Date.==` uses) as a 17-significant-digit string and reconstruct via `Date(timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate:)`; `parseISO8601` parses Double first and falls back to legacy ISO-8601 rows so pre-existing databases still load. verifyReadBack unaffected (does not compare dates).
timestamp_precision_regression_fixed_202.introduced_by: My Phase-2 change making SQLite the authoritative ES store: the store rebuilds `document` from `readGraph()` (not from JSON), and created_at/settled_at were bound with whole-second `ISO8601DateFormatter`.
timestamp_precision_regression_fixed_202.root_cause_detail: Two-part: (1) whole-second ISO8601 loses fractional seconds; (2) even switching to `timeIntervalSince1970` at 17 digits did NOT fix `Date ==`, because Foundation `Date.==` compares `timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate`, and the +/-978307200 epoch offset is not bit-exact for ~1.7e9 values -> equal 1970 seconds can hide unequal reference bits (bitPattern of timeIntervalSince1970 matched while `Date ==` failed).
timestamp_precision_regression_fixed_202.symptom: testDurableGraphPersistsAcrossStoreInstances FAILED only once app tests could execute: an in-memory store's `document` != a store rebuilt from the authority, even though they PRINT identically (sub-second Date precision lost).
timestamp_precision_regression_fixed_202.test_hygiene: Also fixed non-hermetic pre-existing tests: they injected a temp storeURL but not dbURL, so all store instances shared the global ~/.simigo authority and collided. Now setUp injects an isolated dbURL per test (production keeps its single shared store).
